mutants.expected_detection: Harness fixes plaintext, iterates over N distinct random keys, records status each time, and asserts all values equal 0x00; this mutant sets status=0x01 whenever key[0] has bit0 set, so status varies with key content and the invariance assertion fails.

Timing side-channel test: harness times repeated invocations under two key distributions (e.g., all-zero-heavy vs all-one-heavy keys) with fixed plaintext and detects a statistically significant difference in mean execution time due to the extra key-dependent busy-wait loop, failing SR2.

SR3 harness cross-checks that no output other than ciphertext ever reflects key bytes; this mutant XORs status with a key byte (masked to a single bit), causing status to correlate with key content across trials, which the exposure test should flag as unauthorized key leakage.

Harness captures stdout/stderr during crypto_kernel execution and fails because a diagnostic trace line is unconditionally printed to stderr every invocation, violating SR4 (no debug output may be produced).

FR1 known-answer test fails: for plaintext=0x00..0x0F and key=0xFF*16, ciphertext[i] computed via AND instead of XOR no longer equals plaintext[i]^key[i], causing the compile_and_run harness's known-answer-vector check to report a mismatch.

Harness FR2 test iterates 100+ random plaintext/key pairs and checks ciphertext[i] == plaintext[i] ^ key[i] for all i in 0..15; this mutant XORs byte 7 with a fixed constant 0x01 in addition to the key, so ciphertext[7] will mismatch the expected value for any random vector where the correct XOR result's bit0 differs, causing FR2 (and FR1 known-answer check) to fail.

Harness checks that status always equals 0x00 for every well-formed 16-byte plaintext/key pair (FR3). With the unconditional assignment to *status removed, status retains whatever indeterminate/uninitialized value happens to be in the caller-provided memory, so it will not reliably equal 0x00 across test vectors, causing FR3 (and likely FR1) to fail.

g++ -std=c++11 -Wall compilation of inputs/crypto_kernel.cpp against the fixed inputs/crypto_kernel.h will fail because the function signature no longer matches the header prototype (extra parameter added), so FR4 (and consequently FR1-FR3 which depend on successful compile_and_run) will fail.
